{"subject":"Cassandra tail latency on the leaderboard cluster","body":"Hi Lior,

Thanks for connecting. Your talk on running 60 self-managed Apache Cassandra nodes for the Kestrel Games leaderboard cluster stuck with me, especially the tail latency and GC/compaction tuning side.

That's the problem ScyllaDB was built around: a shard-per-core C++ architecture with no JVM garbage-collection pauses, so p99 latency stays predictable without the GC tuning work.

If it's useful, I'm happy to share how that design handles a leaderboard-style workload. Just let me know.

Oz
GTM Engineer, ScyllaDB
